assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine synthesis from a harsh, narrow-scope problem into a routine, general operation. Ligand design (bulky biaryl phosphines, hindered alkylphosphines) made it work across substrates. It is among the most used bond-forming reactions in medicinal and process chemistry and a textbook case of a method that changed how chemists build bonds everywhere. The 2010 prize for cross-coupling did not cover C-N coupling, so this is a distinct chemical advance.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic, ligand-controlled general method and its mechanistic understanding in the mid-1990s onward. Kosugi's earlier Pd/tin amide chemistry is a precursor that required stoichiometric tin reagents; I would recognize it in the citation rather than as a laureate, though this is a judgment call about priority.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use, many generations of ligands and precatalysts, and wide industrial adoption (pharmaceutical process routes, materials). Fully mature; recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: How the committee weighs the 2010 cross-coupling prize when judging novelty (I find the novelty clear but others may differ).
Allocation of early priority between Kosugi and the Buchwald and Hartwig groups; I rely on memory and have not verified the precise chronology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Catalytic C-H functionalization aims at the efficiency I value most: fewer steps and no pre-functionalization. The Pd(II)/directing-group and ligand-accelerated approaches, plus Pd(II)/Pd(IV) catalysis, give predictable site-selectivity and are now used in total synthesis and late-stage functionalization in pharma. Yu's ligand-enabled, template-controlled meta and remote activation is a conceptual advance beyond directing-group chemistry.
assessment.attribution: The field is broad. Yu (ligands, templates, enantioselective C(sp3)-H), Sanford (Pd(II)/Pd(IV) and mechanism) and Daugulis (early directed arylation, aminoquinoline directing group) are the clearest decisive contributors in the supplied credit. Hartwig and Smith (borylation) are also prominent, so the three-person limit forces a choice that is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation and steady adoption, but selectivity and generality still depend on substrate and directing group, and many applications are in academic methodology. Maturity is good but less complete than cross-coupling.
uncertainties: Whether the field should be split among Pd-directed, Ir-borylation and Rh/Ru carbene chemistry, which makes one narrow prize configuration unclear.
Actual penetration into industrial manufacturing relative to academic use; I have not checked this.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically encumbered, uncombined Lewis acid and base can heterolytically cleave H2 and activate small molecules without a transition metal. This is a conceptually simple new reactivity principle with metal-free hydrogenation as a demonstrable outcome. It is original and chemically new, which satisfies my test for what was new.
assessment.attribution: Stephan's 2006 report of reversible H2 activation by a phosphine-borane and Erker's related intramolecular and later catalytic work are the two decisive lines. Welch/Stephan and Erker are cleanly identifiable, so a two-laureate configuration is fair.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed, many independent groups, but practical impact on synthesis and industry is modest compared with metal catalysis. Concept is stable; applications are still developing, so timing is acceptable rather than urgent.
uncertainties: Limited industrial adoption relative to conceptual novelty.
Whether others (e.g., Power's earlier main-group H2 activation work) should receive credit; not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened generation of radical intermediates under mild conditions with simple catalysts and now underpins much late-stage and cross-coupling chemistry (including dual Ni/photoredox). Its adoption in discovery chemistry is very broad, which I weigh heavily, and it is chemically new rather than a reapplication of known photochemistry.
assessment.attribution: Credit is diffuse: MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson published in 2008-2011, with König, Nicewicz, Fukuzumi and Melchiorre also central. MacMillan is the person usually cited as decisive but is already a laureate (2021, organocatalysis). The three names I propose from the supplied strings are defensible but the allocation is the main weakness.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed and widely used. Industrial scale-up (flow, large-scale photochemistry) is still maturing, but recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Contested allocation of credit and precedent of a prior prize to MacMillan overlapping with the field.
Reproducibility and scalability of photochemical reactions in process settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable N-heterocyclic and acyclic carbenes overturned the view that carbenes are only transient and gave a ligand class (NHCs) that changed organometallic catalysis, notably in olefin metathesis and cross-coupling, and an organocatalytic platform. Original, clear and chemically fundamental.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo's 1991 crystalline NHC is the key landmark; Bertrand's earlier phosphinocarbene (1988) and later cyclic alkyl amino carbenes are the other defining contribution. Bode, Nolan and Rovis are application-oriented contributors. A two-person prize is a reasonable configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature, decades of validated use, broad commercial availability of NHC ligands and catalysts. Recognition is timely or somewhat late.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 metathesis prize, in which NHC-based catalysts were an improvement and not the prize subject.
Priority between Bertrand's 1988 carbene and Arduengo's 1991 crystalline NHC depends on how the committee defines stable carbene.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptide segments in water, making total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins a practical operation. This solved a long-standing synthetic problem with conceptual simplicity and enabled protein chemistry (modified histones, D-proteins, ubiquitin conjugates).
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson (with Muir) introduced and developed NCL in 1994; Muir extended it to expressed protein ligation. Danishefsky contributed later extensions (desulfurization chemistry, glycoprotein synthesis); Brik and Liu are more recent. Kent, Dawson and Muir is a cleaner configuration than the larger set.
assessment.maturity: Well established over three decades with broad use, though the biggest impact is within chemical biology and a subset of therapeutic protein research, not general synthesis.
uncertainties: Border with biochemistry, where I would ask whether the impact is mainly enabling studies in biology.
Whether Danishefsky's contributions or Dawson's role should displace someone; I have not verified who published first in detail.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate noncanonical amino acids at defined sites using orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs. It is chemically ingenious, combining ligand design and protein evolution, and gives access to protein chemistry that synthetic methods alone could not. Widely used for bioorthogonal handles, crosslinkers and photocaged residues.
assessment.attribution: Schultz (first orthogonal pairs in E. coli and eukaryotes, 2001 onward) and Chin (quadruplet codons, orthogonal ribosomes, whole-genome recoding) are the clearest decisive contributors in the supplied names; Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama are also important, so the allocation is open.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and used broadly; therapeutic and industrial translation still developing. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Border with biology: what is new chemically is the orthogonal pair design and amino-acid chemistry, but the genetic machinery dominates the work.
Several groups reached similar results at similar times, so priority could be disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: RAFT polymerization gives controlled radical polymerization of a very wide range of monomers with thiocarbonylthio chain-transfer agents, enabling block copolymers and defined architectures under conditions that are practical and tolerant of functionality. Wide commercial and academic adoption makes it a general method in the sense I value.
assessment.attribution: The CSIRO group (Rizzardo, Moad, Thang) published the 1998 discovery and developed the mechanism and agent design, which makes this a compact attribution. Competing ATRP (listed separately) and NMP show that credit within controlled radical polymerization could be divided.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely confirmed, with industrial use. Concerns about sulfur end-group handling are practical but do not undermine the discovery.
uncertainties: Competition with ATRP, which could favor a combined or alternative prize for controlled radical polymerization.
Magnitude of industrial impact relative to academic use; I have not verified production volumes.
